project_type: Static personal website — a hand-written 'composition notebook' design (vanilla HTML + one CSS file), being converted to a minimal Jekyll static site with Decap CMS and Vercel serverless OAuth. Deployed on Vercel at benmanoj.com; publish loop (not yet live) is Decap -> commit to main -> GitHub Actions builds _site -> Vercel serves prebuilt output + api/ functions.
language: HTML/CSS/Liquid (Jekyll) + Node.js (Vercel serverless functions) + YAML config
build_system: Jekyll 4.3 (Ruby/Bundler). QUIRK: GitHub Actions (Ruby 3.3 via ruby/setup-ruby) owns the real build and commits _site/ post-push; Vercel does NO build (buildCommand empty, serves prebuilt _site/ + zero-config api/ functions). Alternative B (Vercel runs Ruby) is documented but NOT the primary path.
test_framework: No unit-test framework. Verification = `bundle exec jekyll build` + `bundle exec jekyll serve` + curl HTTP fetches asserting status 200 and notebook markup/classes; plus `ruby -ryaml` YAML validation and `node --check` for JS. See verification_instructions.
test_command: bundle exec jekyll serve (background) then curl the routes; ruby -ryaml YAML checks; node --check api/*.js
verification_instructions: CRITICAL ENV CONSTRAINT verified during exploration: local Ruby is 2.6.10 (below Jekyll 4.3's required >=2.7); there is NO rbenv/rvm/asdf, NO Homebrew, NO Docker on this machine, so a local Jekyll 4.3 `bundle exec jekyll build` CANNOT run as-is. Verification tiers (design §14): Tier A (local, gates this work) = file shape/markup checks and, if a usable Ruby can be obtained, a local build+serve+curl; if only Ruby 2.6 is available, use a Jekyll-3.x-compatible gem set in a throwaway vendor/ purely to render and assert markup (note CI/Ruby 3.3 owns the production 4.3 build). If no usable Ruby can be installed at all, fall back to static YAML/JS/markup-shape assertions and state the build could not run locally — do NOT fabricate a passing build. Tier B (post-push/deploy: /api/auth 302 on preview, Decap handshake, Actions committing _site) is NOT gated here. For a working serve: curl http://localhost:4000/ , /papers/ , /papers/2024-01-01-example-paper/ , /writing/ , /about/ expect 200 + notebook classes; curl /style.css /fonts/Crayonia.ttf /images/bowl.png expect 200; confirm seed paper auto-lists in /papers/ with its year. Validate admin/config.yml and _config.yml as well-formed YAML with required fields. Clean up _site/, .jekyll-cache/, vendor/, and any throwaway Gemfile.lock before committing.
snapshot_or_generated_files: _site/ is the Jekyll build output. It is NOT committed by this workflow — GitHub Actions creates and commits it after the first push to main (primary path). Gemfile.lock is owned by CI (Ruby 3.3); do NOT hand-write it and do NOT commit a throwaway lock generated during local verification. Under Alternative B, _site/ would be git-ignored instead.
environment_constraints: Worktree branch is publish-workflow; NEVER push to origin (NFR-4) — the final merge step only fast-forwards local main, out of scope for these FEATs. Local Ruby 2.6.10 only; no version manager, no Homebrew, no Docker. All relative paths resolve against the parent workspace, so ALWAYS use the absolute worktree path /Users/benjaminmanoj/Documents/benmanoj/.worktrees/publish-workflow. Source notebook files are UNTRACKED and live in the main tree at /Users/benjaminmanoj/Documents/benmanoj/benmanoj.com and /Users/benjaminmanoj/Documents/benmanoj/public/crayonia — copy them in (FEAT-001), do not assume they are already in the worktree. Secrets (OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET) live only in Vercel env vars, never committed; the client secret is used only server-side in api/callback.js.
contribution_requirements: Preserve style.css EXACTLY (NFR-2): new CSS is additive only (a .paper-body block appended). Generated HTML must reproduce the existing notebook markup/classes identically (NFR-1/FR-3) for home, Writing, About; the Papers index body is intentionally replaced by an auto-list (exempt). HTML comment nodes may be dropped. Stage files by name (not git add -A); commit on publish-workflow; never push. The two outstanding design-review MEDIUMs are documentation-level and already folded into the design: (MEDIUM-1) the /api/auth 404 fallback is a fully-qualified `functions.runtime: @vercel/node@3.2.0` recorded in PUBLISHING.md, not a vercel.json key on the primary path; (MEDIUM-2) ordering/`%Y` come from the REQUIRED front-matter `date:` only — Jekyll does NOT derive date from a custom-collection filename, so every paper must carry date:.
key_patterns: Notebook grid (verified in style.css): --line: clamp(2.6rem,3.2vw+2.4vh,5.6rem); --fs-item: calc(var(--line)*0.8); --baseline-drop: 0.22em; --top-gap: calc(var(--line)*4). .line-row { display:flex; align-items:flex-end; height:var(--line); } and .line-row > * { transform: translateY(var(--baseline-drop)); } — the grid aligns via transform, NOT top. Rules are a repeat-y background on .notebook-page starting at --top-gap with period --line. The SVG pencil filter (baseFrequency 0.08, numOctaves 4, seed 7, scale 3) is IDENTICAL across all four source pages, so one _includes/pencil-filter.html reproduces them. .paper-body must set line-height:var(--line) and transform: translateY(calc(var(--baseline-drop) + (var(--line) - 1em)/2)) to land the first prose baseline on a rule (half-leading correction, design §7.2). Title composition is ONE conditional in the base notebook layout: page.title_tag -> elsif page.collection=='papers' -> '{{page.title}} — Benjamin Manoj' -> else page.title. Decap format:frontmatter + a field literally named body writes the document body below the --- front matter. permalink /papers/:name/ maps 2024-01-01-example-paper.md -> /papers/2024-01-01-example-paper/.
relevant_files: /Users/benjaminmanoj/Documents/benmanoj/benmanoj.com/index.html (SOURCE home; literal page numbers 1/2/3; 15 trailing blank rows)
